primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Any person who has been arrested on a violation of a city ordinance may petition the court to expunge the arrest record. The petition is directed to the municipal court of the city whose ordinance was charged.
When the petition is filed the court sets a hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency.

At the hearing the court shall order the arrest record and subsequent court proceedings expunged on finding any of the following: mistaken identity; that a court found no probable cause for the arrest; that the petitioner was found not guilty; that the arrest was for a violation of an ordinance prohibited by K.S.A. 12-16,134(a) or (b) adopted before July 1, 2014; or that expungement would be in the best interests of justice and charges have been dismissed or no charges have been or are likely to be filed.
The official court file is separated from other court records and disclosed only to a judge, designated court staff, the prosecuting attorney, the arresting agency, or others by court order.
A municipal court may prescribe a fee as costs, except that no fee may be charged to a person arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft.

counselFlags: Court-specific instrument: Kansas has hundreds of municipal courts and no unified municipal forms regime, so the instrument is court-specific even though the mechanism is statewide. Confirm with the municipal court whether it publishes its own expungement form or requires its own process before filing this document.

Charter ordinance risk: some Kansas cities govern expungement by charter ordinance rather than by K.S.A. 12-4516a directly. A bounded sample confirmed that Wichita proceeds under Charter Ordinance No. 224 and publishes its own Motion and Order. Where a city proceeds by charter ordinance, this petition may be the wrong instrument entirely.

The city is never guessed. The city whose ordinance was charged is left as a confirm-with-the-court value in the caption and court name, because naming the wrong municipal court would misdirect the filing.
No waiting period applies. K.S.A. 12-4516a states none; relief turns entirely on establishing one of the statutory grounds.

The statutory grounds are the court's to find, never the petitioner's to assert. This pleading identifies which ground the petitioner relies on and asks the court to find it; it never states that the court has found it.

Notice is the court's act: when the petition is filed the court sets the hearing date and causes notice to be given to the prosecuting attorney and the arresting law enforcement agency. The participant does not serve anyone, and neither the prosecuting attorney's nor the arresting agency's position is ever asserted.

Kansas municipal verification: K.S.A. 12-4516a as described by the source imposes no verification or notarization requirement and identifies no verification statute. Confirm what the municipal court requires before signing; the source does not specify one.

Fee: a municipal court may prescribe a fee as costs under K.S.A. 12-4516a(f), but no amount is established by the source and no amount may be stated to a participant. Ask the municipal court what it charges. No fee may be charged to a person arrested as a result of being a victim of identity theft — a participant in that position should say so to the court.

Wrong-track risk: a municipal conviction or a fulfilled municipal diversion runs under K.S.A. 12-4516, not this section, and an arrest on a state law violation runs under K.S.A. 22-2410 in the district court. Confirm the disposition before using this petition.

The 'best interests of justice' ground requires that charges have been dismissed or that no charges have been or are likely to be filed. Whether charges are 'likely to be filed' is a judgment about the prosecutor's future conduct and must never be asserted by LegalEase; any pending or possible charge should trigger attorney review.

caption.detail: Municipal court caption naming the city whose ordinance was charged. The city is deliberately left as a confirm-with-the-court bracket value rather than guessed.

court_party_identity.detail: The sovereign party is the city (Plaintiff), not the State of Kansas — a municipal ordinance prosecution is brought by the city. The movant is the Petitioner. The prosecuting attorney and arresting law enforcement agency are named by role only as the recipients of the court's notice; no position is asserted for either.

requested_relief.detail: Expunge the arrest record identified in the Petition and the subsequent court proceedings relating to it — the scope K.S.A. 12-4516a(c) confers and no wider.

verification.detail: Signed declaration only. The source imposes no verification or notarization requirement and identifies no verification statute, so none is asserted (citation null + recorded silence + counsel flag).

signatures.detail: Petitioner signature and date blocks; the judge's signature block on the proposed order stays blank for the court.

proposed_order.detail: Proposed order of expungement, filed with the petition. K.S.A. 12-4516a(c) requires the court to order expungement on finding a statutory ground, and the bounded Kansas sample records a municipal Motion and Order practice.

certificate_of_service.detail: Absent by design: under K.S.A. 12-4516a(b) the court sets the hearing date and causes notice to be given. The participant serves no one.

notice_affidavit.detail: Absent by design: notice is the court's act under K.S.A. 12-4516a(b). The source prescribes no participant notice or affidavit document.

filing_instructions.detail: Confirm the municipal court's own practice first, then file the petition and proposed order with that court. The court sets the hearing and gives notice. A fee may be prescribed as costs; its amount is not established and must be confirmed with the court.
